newsitem.title: BURMA: Senior Japanese official visits Burma.
newsitem.headline: Senior Japanese official visits Burma.

text.p: A senior Japanese envoy was due to arrive in Rangoon late on Wednesday for a three-day visit that Burmese officials hoped would lead to a thaw in Burmese-Japanese relations.

Japanese embassy officials said Hiroshi Irabayashi, Japan's cabinet chief councillor for external affairs, was on Thursday scheduled to call on Khin Nyunt, the powerful Secretary One of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
Other details of the envoy's visit were not available.

Analysts in Rangoon said Irabayashi's visit might help improve sluggish Burmese-Japanese ties, which have been strained since Tokyo froze all aid except debt relief grants to Burma after the military seized power in 1988.
Irabayashi's visit followed one last week by Koichi Oka, director of the Japan-Myanmar (Burma) Friendship Association.
Oka said about 30 Japanese businessmen would visit Burma in November with a plan to form a Myanmar-Japan Friendship Association.
